title: Workbench: Error Diagnostics for Timeouts & 5xx - UX notes and wireframes
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures UX notes, quick wireframe writeups, and an initial prioritized grooming backlog for a dedicated 'Error Diagnostics' workbench inside the Console. Focus: timeouts, HTTP 5xx from the runtime, and model-level errors (OOM, tokenization failures, nan/inf activations). Aim is a fast path for engineers and support to triage, reproduce, and remediate production errors without leaving the Console.

Goals / user stories (tl;dr):
- Support engineer: filter error traffic and find the highest-impact root causes in < 5 min.
- Product engineer: compare two failed runs and see diff of inputs, model variant, sequence length, and kernel/quant status.
- Customer support: generate a sanitized repro bundle to attach to a bug or to send to an enterprise customer.

High-level UX components (wireframe building blocks):
1) Error Summary Panel (top header strip)
   - Aggregate KPIs: error rate, p50/p95 error latency, top error classes (Timeout, 5xx, ModelError).
   - Time selector (last 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, custom).
   - Quick links: open incident, create support bundle, export CSV.

2) Error Feed (left column)
   - List of individual error events ordered by severity then time. Each row shows: timestamp, route, model name@version, error code, duration, request id, customer id (if available).
   - Inline tags for suspected root cause (network, infra, model, quota). Tags are auto-suggested by heuristics.
   - Row interactions: expand for request details, mark as acknowledged, mute group, create Jira.

3) Request Inspector (central pane)
   - Tabbed view: Overview | Raw Request | Timeline & Traces | Model Output | Replay / Rerun.
   - Overview: Shows request metadata and inferred signals (token_count, kernel selection, quantization flag, GPU id, host).
   - Raw Request: sanitized prompt, params, headers. Toggle to show PII-scrubbed or original (enterprise only).
   - Timeline & Traces: visual waterfall of phases (ingest -> routing -> runtime -> kernel init -> generation -> postprocess). Hover shows durations and logs. Integrates with trace ids (OpenTelemetry).
   - Model Output: when present, show final output + error stack (e.g., OOM: staged buffer exceed). For timeouts, show last partial tokens and kv-cache state snapshot size.
   - Replay / Rerun: button to run the same request against a selectable model variant/quantization setting with isolation (dry-run mode that doesn't count against customer usage). Results appear inline, diffable.

4) Error Grouping & Swimlanes (right column / bottom ribbon)
   - Automatic groups by signature (route + model + error-code + input-hash prefix).
   - Swimlane visualization: each lane = error class. Zoom to see bursty episodes.
   - Quick actions on group: escalate, annotate (internal notes), create release-blocker, pin.

5) Root-cause Indicators (small badges and signals)
   - Green / amber / red indicators derived from heuristics: hot-shard (GPU), memory-pressure, model-variant-rollback, recent rollout, kernel-failure, upstream-network. Clicking indicator filters the feed to matching events.

Wireframe notes (low-fidelity):
- Single page: three-column layout (Left: feed ~25%, Center: inspector ~50%, Right: groups + actions ~25%).
- Mobile: feed-first, inspector opens full-screen modal.
- Visual language: compact rows, monospace for IDs and logs, small sparklines for latencies.
- Colors: use brand accent but reserve red for actionable severity only.

Heuristics and detection rules (engineering input):
- Timeout detection: request duration >= user SLO threshold OR runtime didn't emit 'generation_end' but kernel logs show last token timestamp. Mark as "generation timeout".
- 5xx classification: map 5xx subcodes to categories (OOM, kernel crash, internal service, routing).
- ModelError detection: parse runtime stderr for flagged signatures (e.g., "OutOfMemoryError", "Tensor NaN encountered", "TokenizerError").
- Group signature derivation: hash of sanitized prompt prefix (first 256 chars) + model_name + error_code + quant_flag.

Backlog (prioritized grooming list):
- INF-3421 Implement feed row expansion + inline actions (ack, mute, create-jira) -- M / Spike 2d -- Acceptance: expand shows full metadata and buttons create ticket prefills.
- INF-3478 Timeline & trace integration with OpenTelemetry traces -- H / 1 sprint -- Acceptance: waterfall links to trace UI, hover shows spans and span durations.
- INF-3512 Replay sandbox for reruns (dry-run mode) -- H / 2 sprints -- Acceptance: rerun against alternate model returns deterministic response and diff UI shows token-level differences.
- INF-3550 Auto-grouping tuning & heuristics dashboard -- M / 4 days -- Acceptance: grouping matches >80% of manual groupings on sample dataset.
- INF-3601 Root-cause badges and filter shortcuts -- L / grooming -- Acceptance: clicking badge applies filters and updates feed.
- INF-3667 Support-bundle export (sanitization toggle) -- H / 1 sprint -- Acceptance: bundle contains request, minimal logs, trace id and can be downloaded as ZIP.

Open design questions / risks:
- Privacy: how to expose raw prompts in multi-tenant environment; enterprise-only toggle and audit trail required.
- Cost: replay sandbox could be abused; need per-account limits and dry-run metering.
- Noise: auto-grouping must avoid overfitting; provide simple opt-out to group by route only.
- Rollouts: we need to surface recent model rollouts and configuration changes (console has this data) and correlate with spikes.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics for MVP:
- Time-to-first-insight: median time for an engineer to identify a probable root cause reduces from 25m to <= 7m in lab tests.
- Repro bundle adoption: support team uses export for >= 60% of escalations in first 3 months.
- False grouping rate: <20% false positives for auto-groups on a labeled dataset.

Mockup walkthrough (scenario):
1) Ops receives alert: elevated 5xx for /v1/generate in the last 10m.
2) Open Workbench -> Auto-filter shows group "5xx - OOM - model-7b-quant" with 42 events.
3) Click group -> feed shows representative event -> open inspector -> Timeline shows a long kernel init followed by OOM. Root-cause badges show memory-pressure + recent rollout.
4) Click "Replay" to run against model-7b-quant-smaller-batch, verify success, mark as workaround, create Jira INF-3512 to track permanent mitigation.

Low priority / nice-to-have ideas (future):
- ML-assisted root cause explanations (short natural language summary and recommended remediations).
- Heatmap of GPU-level memory over time correlated with error spikes.
- Auto-pause for model variants that exceed error thresholds.

Next steps (owner actions):
- Design: produce mid-fidelity mockups for the three primary panes (due 2026-03-20) -- Asha.
- Eng: spike on safe rerun sandbox (2 engineers, 1 week) -- Liam.
- Product: map policy decisions for prompt visibility (legal sign-off) -- Sofia.

Notes / links:
- See FIGMA: workbench-error-diagnostics (linked above) for initial layout.
- Related tickets: INF-3200 (rollout correlation), INF-3081 (console trace linking).

Comments (notes to self):
- Keep feed lightweight; most time should be spent in the inspector.
- Consider a keyboard-first workflow for rapid triage (j/k/n hotkeys).
- Demo plan: show a 5-minute triage in next PM sync.
